nodes.title: Double integral over a rectangle
nodes.formula:
$∬_R f dA = ∫_a^b ∫_c^d f dy dx$
Area $= ∬_R 1 dA$
Volume $= ∬_R f dA$ when $f ≥ 0$
If $f = g(x) h(y)$: $∫_a^b g dx · ∫_c^d h dy$
Cross-section $A(x) = ∫_c^d f(x, y) dy$
$V = ∫_a^b A(x) dx$
steps: Pick the order with the easy inner integral. For $x e^{xy}$, do $dy$ first.
Integrate the inner variable and hold the other one constant.
Integrate the outer variable.

nodes.title: Double integral over a general region
nodes.formula:
Type I: $∫_a^b ∫_{g_1(x)}^{g_2(x)} f dy dx$
Type II: $∫_c^d ∫_{h_1(y)}^{h_2(y)} f dx dy$
Line through two points:
  $y = y_1 + m(x − x_1)$
Between surfaces: $∬_D (\text{top} − \text{bottom}) dA$
steps: Sketch the region and find where the curves meet.
A vertical line always enters and leaves through the same curves → Type I. Horizontal → Type II.
If neither works, split at the corner and add.
Outer limits are numbers. Inner limits are curves.
nodes.warn: Choose the type that avoids splitting.

nodes.title: Reverse the order
nodes.formula:
$∫_0^1 ∫_{x^2}^1 f dy dx = ∫_0^1 ∫_0^{\sqrt{y}} f dx dy$
$y = x^2 ⟺ x = \sqrt{y}$
$x = arcsin y ⟺ y = sin x$
$x = ln y ⟺ y = e^x$
nodes.body: Use it when the inner integral can't be done, like $e^{x^2}$, $sin(y^2)$ or $\sqrt{1 + x^3}$.
steps: Write the limits as inequalities and sketch the region.
New outer variable: its smallest to largest value.
Solve each boundary for the new inner variable.
Inner limits run from the curve you enter to the curve you leave.
nodes.warn: Never just swap dx and dy.

nodes.title: Polar coordinates
nodes.formula:
$x = r cos θ$,  $y = r sin θ$
$x^2 + y^2 = r^2$
$dA = r dr dθ$
$∬_D f dA = ∫_α^β ∫_{r_1}^{r_2} f(r cos θ, r sin θ) r dr dθ$
steps: Convert the region and the integrand.
Multiply by the extra $r$.
Integrate $dr$ first, then $dθ$.

nodes.title: Polar limits
nodes.formula:
Disk: $0 ≤ r ≤ R$,  $0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π$
Ring: $R_1 ≤ r ≤ R_2$
Quadrant I: $0 ≤ θ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$
Upper half: $0 ≤ θ ≤ π$
Right half: $−\frac{π}{2} ≤ θ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$
Line $y = mx$: $θ = arctan m$
  $y = x → \frac{π}{4}$,  $y = \sqrt{3} x → \frac{π}{3}$
$x^2 + y^2 = 2ax$: $r = 2a cos θ$
$x^2 + y^2 = 2ay$: $r = 2a sin θ$
$y = c$: $r = c csc θ$,  $x = c$: $r = c sec θ$
nodes.body: Angles go counterclockwise and may start negative, like $−\frac{π}{4}$ to $\frac{3π}{4}$.

nodes.title: Area inside r = g(θ)
nodes.formula: $A = ∫_α^β ∫_0^{g(θ)} r dr dθ = ∫_α^β \frac{1}{2} g(θ)^2 dθ$
nodes.body: Read the θ limits from where the curve starts and ends in the picture.

nodes.title: Converting from x and y
nodes.formula:
$y$ from $0$ to $\sqrt{R^2 − x^2}$ → upper half-disk
$x$ from $−\sqrt{R^2 − y^2}$ to $\sqrt{R^2 − y^2}$ → full disk
$y$ from $0$ to $\sqrt{2ax − x^2}$ →
  $0 ≤ r ≤ 2a cos θ$,  $0 ≤ θ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$
$\sqrt{x^2 + y^2} → r$,  $x^2 + y^2 → r^2$
nodes.body: Sketch the region from the limits first, then write polar limits.

nodes.title: Surface area
nodes.formula:
$A = ∬_D \sqrt{1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2} dA$
Plane $ax + by + cz = d$:
  $A = \frac{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}}{|c|} · \text{Area}(D)$
Sphere: $\sqrt{1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{a^2 − r^2}}$
Paraboloid $z = x^2 + y^2$: $\sqrt{1 + 4r^2}$
Parametric: $A = ∬_D |\bf{r}_u × \bf{r}_v| du dv$
steps: $D$ is the shadow on the $xy$-plane. Inside $x^2 + y^2 = R^2$ means a disk.
If the root has $x^2 + y^2$, switch to polar and keep the $r$.
If the root is a constant, multiply it by the area of $D$.
nodes.warn: Keep the 1 inside the square root.

nodes.title: Triple integral
nodes.formula:
$∭_E f dV = ∬_D ∫_{u_1}^{u_2} f dz dA$
$V = ∬_D (\text{top} − \text{bottom}) dA$
Tetrahedron $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} + \frac{z}{c} = 1$:
  $0 ≤ z ≤ c(1 − \frac{x}{a} − \frac{y}{b})$
  $0 ≤ y ≤ b(1 − \frac{x}{a})$,  $0 ≤ x ≤ a$
  $V = \frac{abc}{6}$
steps: The inner variable is the one with a clear floor and ceiling, usually $z$.
Find the shadow $D$: set top = bottom and add any walls.
Describe $D$ as a Type I or Type II region.
nodes.warn: A limit can only use variables that are integrated later.

nodes.title: Change the order
steps: Write all six inequalities and sketch the solid.
Solve each surface for the new inner variable.
Find the shadow on the other two variables by eliminating the inner one.
Describe that shadow in the new order. Split if a boundary changes.

nodes.title: Cylindrical coordinates
nodes.formula:
$x = r cos θ$,  $y = r sin θ$,  $z = z$
$dV = r dz dr dθ$
Cylinder $x^2 + y^2 = R^2$ → $r = R$
Cone $z = k\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ → $z = kr$
Paraboloid $z = a ± (x^2 + y^2)$ → $z = a ± r^2$
Sphere → $z = ±\sqrt{R^2 − r^2}$
Plane $z = y$ → $z = r sin θ$
$x^2 + y^2 = 2ax$ → $r = 2a cos θ$
steps: $z$ runs from the bottom surface to the top surface.
$r$ runs from 0 to the edge of the shadow, where top = bottom or a wall.
$θ$ runs from 0 to $2π$ unless the solid is cut.
nodes.warn: Don't forget the extra r. The cone z = r is above the paraboloid z = r² when r < 1.

nodes.title: Paraboloid along the x-axis
nodes.formula:
Paraboloid $x = a(y^2 + z^2)$, plane $x = c$
$y = r cos θ$,  $z = r sin θ$
$ar^2 ≤ x ≤ c$,  $0 ≤ r ≤ \sqrt{\frac{c}{a}}$
$dV = r dx dr dθ$
nodes.body: An integrand of $x$ stays $x$. Do the same for the $y$-axis using $x$ and $z$.

nodes.title: Spherical coordinates
nodes.formula:
$x = ρ sin φ cos θ$
$y = ρ sin φ sin θ$
$z = ρ cos φ$
$ρ^2 = x^2 + y^2 + z^2$
$dV = ρ^2 sin φ dρ dφ dθ$
$0 ≤ φ ≤ π$,  $0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π$
steps: $ρ$ runs from the origin out to the surface. It may depend on $φ$.
$φ$ is measured down from the positive $z$-axis.
With constant limits, split into three single integrals.
nodes.warn: Include ρ² sin φ. φ is from the z-axis; θ goes around it.

nodes.title: Spherical limits
nodes.formula:
Ball: $0 ≤ ρ ≤ R$,  $0 ≤ φ ≤ π$,  $0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π$
Upper half: $0 ≤ φ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$
First octant: $0 ≤ φ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$,  $0 ≤ θ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$
Inside sphere, above cone: $0 ≤ φ ≤ φ_0$
Outside cone, above $xy$-plane: $φ_0 ≤ φ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$
Shell: $R_1 ≤ ρ ≤ R_2$
$x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 2az$ → $ρ ≤ 2a cos φ$
Below the plane $z = h$ → $ρ ≤ h sec φ$
Cap above $z = h$: $h sec φ ≤ ρ ≤ R$
  $0 ≤ φ ≤ arccos \frac{h}{R}$

nodes.title: Cones and surfaces
nodes.formula:
$z = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ → $φ = \frac{π}{4}$
$z = \sqrt{3} \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ → $φ = \frac{π}{6}$
$z = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ → $φ = \frac{π}{3}$
$z = k \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ → $tan φ = \frac{1}{k}$
Sphere of radius $R$ → $ρ = R$
Plane $z = h$ → $ρ = h sec φ$
Cylinder $x^2 + y^2 = a^2$ → $ρ = a csc φ$

nodes.title: Mass & centroid
nodes.formula:
$m = ∬_D δ dA$
$M_y = ∬_D x δ dA$,  $M_x = ∬_D y δ dA$
$\bar{x} = \frac{M_y}{m}$,  $\bar{y} = \frac{M_x}{m}$
Solid: $m = ∭_E δ dV$
  $\bar{z} = \frac{1}{m} ∭_E z δ dV$
Average: $f_{avg} = \frac{1}{\text{Area}} ∬_D f dA$
steps: Use symmetry first. Round about the $z$-axis means $\bar{x} = \bar{y} = 0$.
With constant density, it cancels: use the volume or area for $m$.
In spherical, $z = ρ cos φ$, so the integrand becomes $ρ^3 sin φ cos φ$.
nodes.warn: The centroid has to land inside the solid.

choices.label: Example: cone in a shifted sphere

nodes.title: Cone in a shifted sphere
nodes.formula:
Sphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 2z$, cone $φ = \frac{π}{4}$
$0 ≤ ρ ≤ 2 cos φ$,  $0 ≤ φ ≤ \frac{π}{4}$
$V = 2π ∫_0^{π/4} \frac{8 cos^3 φ}{3} sin φ dφ = π$
$M_{xy} = 2π ∫_0^{π/4} 4 cos^5 φ sin φ dφ = \frac{7π}{6}$
$\bar{z} = \frac{7}{6}$

nodes.title: Line integral of f ds
nodes.formula:
$∫_C f ds = ∫_a^b f(\bf{r}(t)) |\bf{r}'(t)| dt$
$ds = \sqrt{x'^2 + y'^2 + z'^2} dt$
Mass $= ∫_C δ ds$,  length $= ∫_C ds$
$∫_C f dx = ∫_a^b f(\bf{r}(t)) x'(t) dt$
steps: Parameterize the curve as $\bf{r}(t)$.
Find the speed $|\bf{r}'(t)|$.
Substitute and integrate in $t$.
nodes.warn: ds needs the speed. dx and dy don't.

nodes.title: Parameterizations
nodes.formula:
Segment: $\bf{r}(t) = A + t(B − A)$,  $0 ≤ t ≤ 1$
Circle: $(a cos t, a sin t)$,  $0 ≤ t ≤ 2π$
Ellipse: $(a cos t, b sin t)$
Graph $y = g(x)$: $(t, g(t))$
Graph $x = g(y)$: $(g(t), t)$
Helix: $(cos t, sin t, t)$
nodes.body: For a path made of pieces, do each piece and add.

nodes.title: Work along a path
nodes.formula:
$W = ∫_C \bf{F} · d\bf{r} = ∫_a^b \bf{F}(\bf{r}(t)) · \bf{r}'(t) dt$
  $= ∫_C P dx + Q dy + R dz$
$∫_{−C} \bf{F} · d\bf{r} = −∫_C \bf{F} · d\bf{r}$
steps: Look for a shortcut: a closed curve in the plane → Green; $∇ × \bf{F} = \bf{0}$ → potential.
Otherwise parameterize, dot $\bf{F}(\bf{r}(t))$ with $\bf{r}'(t)$, and integrate.
To match a picture: the arrow at $\bf{r}(t)$ is $\bf{F}(\bf{r}(t))$.
nodes.warn: It's a dot product, not a magnitude.

nodes.title: Conservative fields
steps: $f = ∫ P dx + g(y, z)$
Match $f_y = Q$ to find $g$.
Match $f_z = R$ to find $h(z)$.
The answer is $f(\text{end}) − f(\text{start})$.

nodes.title: Green's theorem
nodes.formula:
$∮_C P dx + Q dy = ∬_D (\frac{∂Q}{∂x} − \frac{∂P}{∂y}) dA$
Counterclockwise is positive. Clockwise: flip the sign.
Area $= ∮_C x dy = −∮_C y dx$
  $= \frac{1}{2} ∮_C (x dy − y dx)$
steps: $P$ multiplies $dx$, $Q$ multiplies $dy$.
Integrate $\frac{∂Q}{∂x} − \frac{∂P}{∂y}$ over the region inside.
If that's a constant $k$, the answer is $k$ times the area.
To check directly, parameterize each edge and add.
nodes.warn: It's ∂Q/∂x − ∂P/∂y, Q first. The curve must be closed.

nodes.title: Gradient, divergence, curl
nodes.body:
Gradient: scalar → vector
Divergence: vector → scalar
Curl: vector → vector
Laplacian: scalar → scalar
nodes.warn: In the curl, the middle part is P_z − R_x.

nodes.title: Does it make sense?
nodes.body:
Work from the inside out and track scalar or vector.
Makes sense: div(grad f), curl(grad f), grad(div F), div(curl F), curl(curl F).
Nonsense: curl(div F), div(div F), grad(grad f), grad F, div f.

nodes.title: Points & solids
nodes.formula:
Cylindrical $(r, θ, z)$ →
  $(r cos θ, r sin θ, z)$
Spherical $(ρ, θ, φ)$ →
  $(ρ sin φ cos θ, ρ sin φ sin θ, ρ cos φ)$
$r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$,  $tan θ = \frac{y}{x}$
$ρ = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}$,  $cos φ = \frac{z}{ρ}$
nodes.body:
$0 ≤ θ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$ means $x, y ≥ 0$. $0 ≤ θ ≤ π$ means $y ≥ 0$.
$r ≤ z$ or $φ ≤ \frac{π}{2}$ means $z ≥ 0$.
$z = c$ is a plane, $z = r$ a cone, $ρ = c$ a sphere, $φ = c$ a cone.
nodes.warn: Spherical points are written (ρ, θ, φ), with θ second.

nodes.title: Symmetry gives zero
nodes.body:
If $D$ is symmetric across the $y$-axis and $f(−x, y) = −f(x, y)$, then $∬_D f dA = 0$.
So $∬ x dA = 0$ and $∬ x y^2 dA = 0$ over a disk.
A solid that's round about the $z$-axis has $\bar{x} = \bar{y} = 0$.
$∫_0^{2π} sin θ dθ = ∫_0^{2π} cos θ dθ = 0$

nodes.title: Choosing the order
nodes.body:
Constant limits and $f = g(x) h(y)$: split into a product of two integrals.
For $x e^{xy}$ or $x cos(xy)$, integrate $dy$ first.
If the inner integral is impossible, like $e^{x^2}$, reverse the order.
Pick the order that avoids splitting the region.

nodes.title: Known areas & volumes
nodes.formula:
Disk $πR^2$,  sector $\frac{1}{2} R^2 θ$
Ellipse $πab$,  triangle $\frac{1}{2} bh$
Triangle from its corners:
  $\frac{1}{2} |x_1(y_2 − y_3) + x_2(y_3 − y_1) + x_3(y_1 − y_2)|$
Ball $\frac{4}{3} πR^3$,  hemisphere $\frac{2}{3} πR^3$
Cone $\frac{1}{3} πR^2 h$,  cylinder $πR^2 h$
Half-cylinder $\frac{1}{2} πR^2 L$
nodes.body: If $f ≥ 0$ and the solid is a familiar shape, skip the integral.

nodes.title: Trig identities & values
nodes.formula:
$sin^2 θ = \frac{1 − cos 2θ}{2}$
$cos^2 θ = \frac{1 + cos 2θ}{2}$
$sin θ cos θ = \frac{1}{2} sin 2θ$
$∫_0^{2π} sin^2 θ dθ = ∫_0^{2π} cos^2 θ dθ = π$
$∫_0^{π/2} sin^2 θ dθ = \frac{π}{4}$
$∫_0^π sin φ dφ = 2$,  $∫_0^{π/2} sin φ dφ = 1$
$∫_0^{π/4} sin φ dφ = 1 − \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$
$∫_0^{π/2} sin^3 φ dφ = \frac{2}{3}$
$cos \frac{π}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$,  $sin \frac{π}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$
$cos \frac{π}{4} = sin \frac{π}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$
nodes.body: Odd power: save one factor, turn the rest into cosines with $sin^2 = 1 − cos^2$, then let $u = cos θ$.

nodes.title: Substitution patterns
nodes.body: For $∫ ρ^3 e^{ρ^2} dρ$, let $u = ρ^2$, then integrate by parts.

nodes.title: Integration by parts
nodes.formula:
$∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du$
$∫ x e^x dx = (x − 1) e^x$
$∫ x cos x dx = x sin x + cos x$
$∫ x sin x dx = sin x − x cos x$
$∫ ln x dx = x ln x − x$
nodes.body: Pick u in this order: log, inverse trig, algebraic, trig, exponential.

nodes.title: Line integral rules
nodes.body:
Reversing the path flips the sign of $∫ \bf{F} · d\bf{r}$ but not of $∫ f ds$.
$∫ g(x) dx$ on its own depends only on the $x$ endpoints.
A conservative field around a closed loop gives 0.
Speed on a circle of radius $a$ is $a$. On a segment it's $|B − A|$.
A field pointing mostly along the motion does positive work.

nodes.title: Sanity checks
nodes.body:
Jacobian: $r$ for polar and cylindrical, $ρ^2 sin φ$ for spherical.
Outer limits are numbers, and lower is below upper.
Volume, area, mass and length come out positive.
The centroid lands inside the solid.
A clockwise or reversed path flips the sign.
Angles are in radians.
A triangle's area has the $\frac{1}{2}$.

choices.label: Q6–9  Type I and Type II
Q20, 24  Orders of a triple integral
